subject: MSA redline: exit slate, commencement timing, and notice windows
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MSA redline submission — exit slate & commencement timing

Hi team — attaching MSA v3 with our proposed redlines focused on term and exit mechanics. High-level asks below so procurement/legal can triage quickly: 

- Auto-renew: keep 12-month renewal periods but add a 60-day notice window to opt-out for pilots (we can discuss different tiers for enterprise commits).
- Termination for convenience (TFC): propose a 60-day TFC for pilot and early-stage contracts; for committed ARR > $500k propose 90 days + transition support.
- Commencement / Go-live: define commencement as the first production API call (rather than signing date) to avoid start-date disputes.
- Refund / pro-ration: if they terminate TFC within the first 120 days, pro-rate the unused pre-paid portion and waive final month fees for pilots.

Attachments: redline_msa_v3.pdf (pdf), orderform_draft.xlsx (xlsx)

Next steps: can Acme confirm whether procurement prefers a single set of redlines or a two-track (pilot vs enterprise) approach? If helpful, we can do a 30-min legal call this week — Laura and Markus will join.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Acme Legal <legalops@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline submission — exit slate & commencement timing

Thanks for the redline, Aditya. A few initial reactions from legal: 

- 60-day TFC is shorter than Acme policy for platform contracts; our standard is 90 days plus reasonable transition assistance.
- We cannot accept a definition of commencement tied to the first production API call without a clear carveout for staging/validation windows — procurement needs date certainty for billing and audit.
- Pro-ration and waiving fees for early termination need precise definitions (what counts as "pilot", when does the 120-day clock start).

Can you provide a clear matrix that maps: commitment size -> notice window -> TFC length -> transition SLA? That will help procurement sign off. Also please identify the internal legal contact to join a redline sync; we prefer to loop in our commercial contracts lead.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline submission — exit slate & commencement timing

Hi — thanks for the quick review and good questions. I pulled together a short matrix (attached as termination_matrix.csv) that maps commitment tiers to recommended notice/TFC/transition SLAs. Key points: 

- Pilot tier (no minimum ARR, evaluation customers): 60-day notice, 45-day TFC, limited transition assistance (handover docs + export of data).
- Standard tier (committed ARR <$500k): 60-day notice, 60-day TFC, 60 days of transition assistance with a nominal handover fee to cover data egress if significant engineering support required.
- Enterprise tier (committed ARR >=$500k): 90-day notice, 90-day TFC, 90 days of transition assistance with a standard ramp/handover schedule and an option for paid extended support.

On commencement: we are proposing a hybrid approach — COMMENCEMENT = (earlier of signed order form OR agreed go-live window) but with an explicit "acceptance" carveout: a 14-day validation/staging period after the first production call during which either party can flag unresolved integration defects and pause billing. This is intended to give Acme the date certainty you want while protecting Redwood for pilot usage.

Suggested next step: 30-min call to walk redlines and the matrix. Are you available Wed Mar 4 10:00–10:30 PT or Thu Mar 5 09:00–09:30 PT? Laura (commercial counsel) and Markus (senior legal) will attend.

Attachment: termination_matrix.csv (csv)

Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline submission — exit slate & commencement timing (summary & next steps)

Team — quick recap and alignment from today's sync (thanks everyone for joining). We landed on a compromise that should keep both sides operationally predictable: 

- Notice: 75-day blended notice window (implemented as: 60 days for pilot/standard; 90 days for enterprise; with a single clause expressing "either party may provide written notice not less than 75 days prior to termination for convenience" to simplify billing systems).
- TFC: 75-day termination for convenience as a baseline; tiered service credits/transition assistance to be spelled out on the order form. Pilot carveout: 45-day TFC with pro-rated refund for unused pre-paid fees if termination occurs within the first 120 days.
- Commencement: use the hybrid definition Laura proposed: earlier of signed order form or agreed go-live window, with a 14-day validation period after first production call that pauses certain billing triggers for unresolved integration defects.

Action items: 
1) Redwood (Aditya + Laura) to deliver an updated tracked redline (redline_msa_v3.pdf updated) and a one-page matrix for the order form by EOD Wed Mar 8.
2) Acme procurement to confirm whether they need a separate purchase order or if the attached orderform_draft.xlsx is sufficient; please respond by Fri Mar 12.
3) Legal to exchange final markups and aim for mutual sign-off by Mar 22 so procurement can process the FY28 quarter booking.

Attachments: redline_msa_v3.pdf (updated with tracked changes), orderform_draft.xlsx (status: draft).

Please reply on thread if anything above is incorrect. If acceptable, Aditya, please kick off the DocuSign envelope once final redline is confirmed.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
